0.translation: See [Flagship data sources and construction](⟦shared:0⟧) for provenance, display selections and rebuilding. This page loads bundled inputs directly and focuses on plotting settings.

1.translation: Start with observed HSPs from one sequence pair, then extend to a four-sequence matrix. The minimal inputs are complete sequence lengths and four HSP endpoints; annotations are optional.

5.translation: The bundled PAF table retains 11 observed HSPs for one pair. The recorded full lengths determine the axes. Normalized reverse target intervals retain descending coordinates.

6.translation:
Each line runs from ⟦shared:0⟧ to ⟦shared:1⟧. ⟦shared:2⟧ is not
required. Use ⟦shared:3⟧ mappings and scales for colour, alpha, width and type.
The default Identity domain is 0–100 with ticks 0/50/80/90/95/100; an explicit
user scale overrides it.

9.translation: Keep the descending endpoints of reverse HSPs. Sorting each interval would change the direction of the original segment.

10.translation:
⟦shared:0⟧ and ⟦shared:1⟧ independently select/order accessions. ⟦shared:2⟧ is display
spacing in native bp/aa, not omitted source sequence. Axis directions accept
1/-1 or complete named vectors. Display reversal changes the slope without
changing the biological source table. Each axis starts at source position 1;
concatenated segments retain their own accession and local tick labels.

12.translation:
Use ⟦shared:0⟧ for native/global conversion,
with ⟦shared:1⟧ to go back. Display gaps return NA. Focused source
origins use ⟦shared:2⟧; default axis labels stay window-relative.
Unknown directions are warned, omitted and reported; contradictory direction
metadata is rejected. Repeated declared HSP IDs require ⟦shared:3⟧
in all participating layers. Unidentified duplicate/self rows remain distinct.
Without cg/cs/CIGAR or another alignment trace, these are HSP segments, not
base-level mismatches or gap paths.

15.translation: The following code directly uses bundled ⟦shared:0⟧, with counts and label tables already prepared. It retains all 32 HSPs across four sequences without inventing self-alignments, symmetric records or missing HSPs. The 266 CDS belong to the shared source table but are not passed to the Dotplot segment layer. Empty regions indicate no relationship records in this input, not an absence of homology.

16.translation: Column headers identify each query sequence and its complete 1–length range; row headers identify subject sequences and ranges. Bottom and right ticks show local positions within each sequence. Follow a column and row to locate a pair. Each outlined rectangle retains widths and heights proportional to the actual lengths. Pale backgrounds distinguish cells and do not encode similarity; spaces between rectangles are display gaps.

17.translation: The input records one query-to-subject direction per unordered pair. An empty cell has no input records. Axis labels, cell boundaries and counts use the bundled data.

22.translation: Relative endpoint direction comes from the source record. Reversing a display axis changes the visible slope while leaving the source direction unchanged. Count the supplied directions per sequence pair:

26.translation: Map the first HSP query start onto the concatenated x ⟦shared:1⟧. Inverse lookup uses ⟦shared:0⟧ and an explicit ⟦shared:1⟧; display gaps return NA. The four endpoints remain unchanged.

30.translation: To facet by directed sequence pair, use ggplot2 row and column facets for the two endpoint IDs. For gap or mismatch information at individual positions, see [character alignments](⟦shared:0⟧).
